docs/external/getting-started.md says any URL scheme other than the listed mysql+pymysql:// and mysql:// fails at config load, but the validator accepts every mysql+<driver>:// URL.
The supported-scheme rule is stated in four places that disagree; factory, preflight and sqlglot_dialect_for_url still accept a bare mysql prefix such as mysqlx:// when config validation is skipped.
DatabaseConfig.dialect returns the scheme's raw case and any sqlite-prefixed text, leaving normalization to callers.
claude-desktop install --dry-run returns a clean plan for a database URL the new scheme check refuses, because the dry run returns before validate_toml.

The new mysql row in test_call_after_nested_comment_markers_is_checked is refused by the nested-comment check before any function lookup, duplicating existing rows.
The MySQL row says the URL requires a database name, but build_sql_runner checks only hostname and username.

## Verdict: REJECT (two Important findings: user-facing docs say valid MySQL URLs are refused)

The PR is not ready to merge, because two published pages this PR rewrote tell users that `mysql+<driver>://` URLs other than `mysql+pymysql://` fail to load, and the new validator accepts them.
Rule applied: rule 3 — a Phase-3 finding at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. `README.md` lines 58-61: the Database URLs table lists only `mysql+pymysql://...` and `mysql://...`, and the next sentence says "Any other URL scheme ... fails every `sqllens` command that loads the config". That is false for every other MySQL driver URL. `DatabaseConfig._supported_url_scheme` in `src/sqllens/config.py` (lines 109-115) accepts any scheme that equals `mysql` or starts with `mysql+`, so `mysql+mysqldb://` and `mysql+mysqlconnector://` load fine, and `tests/unit/test_config_schema.py` pins them as accepted. `docs/external/configuration.md` states the rule correctly as `mysql+<driver>://`. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: rewording the sentence changes no output of the URL validator; git grep -F for README.md across *.sh, *.py, *.jq, *.yml, *.yaml, *.toml, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/ and .prflow/skill-extensions/ finds only pyproject.toml:9 readme metadata and scripts/changelog.py name checks, no behavior reader; README is the published PyPI long description -->
2. `docs/external/getting-started.md` lines 98-101: the same false claim. The table lists only `mysql+pymysql://...` (or `mysql://...`), and line 101 says "Any other URL scheme ... fails at config load", although the validator accepts every `mysql+<driver>://` URL. This is a published external page. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: rewording the sentence changes no output of the URL validator; git grep -F for getting-started.md across *.sh, *.py, *.jq, *.yml, *.yaml, *.toml, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/ and .prflow/skill-extensions/ finds no reader; docs/external is published user documentation -->

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (9)

<details><summary>9 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/config.py` lines 111-116: the supported-scheme rule now lives in four places that do not agree. The config validator accepts only `mysql`, `mysql+...` and `sqlite...`, but `build_sql_runner` (`src/sqllens/agent/factory.py:250`), `probe_database` (`src/sqllens/preflight.py:115`) and `sqlglot_dialect_for_url` (`src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:185-187`) still match a bare `mysql` prefix, so a direct call with `mysqlx://` that skips config validation gets a MySQL runner, a pymysql probe and the `mysql` dialect. Nothing reachable through config is affected today. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/config.py` lines 118-125: `DatabaseConfig.dialect` returns the scheme's raw text while the validator compares it case-insensitively, so `MYSQL+PyMySQL://` gives `"MYSQL"` and `sqlitefoo://` gives `"sqlitefoo"`. The only caller, `compare_sql` in `src/sqllens/eval/runner.py:145`, lowercases it, so behavior is correct today. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/installers/claude_desktop.py` lines 380-390: `claude-desktop install --dry-run` checks `--db` only with SQLAlchemy's `make_url`, and returns its plan (lines 502-519) before `validate_toml` (line 584) runs the new scheme check, so `--db postgresql://... --dry-run` shows a clean plan for a config that `serve` and `validate` refuse. Without `--dry-run` the installer writes the TOML and launcher and then reverts them on a best-effort basis, which contradicts the comment at lines 380-381. The gap predates this PR, but the new URL check makes it easier to hit. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `tests/unit/test_sql_runner_cleanup.py` lines 119-135: the ported "cursor allocation raises" test never reaches the query cursor. `MySQLRunner` defaults to `read_only=True`, so `conn.cursor()` first fails at the read-only setup cursor (`src/sqllens/agent/integrations/mysql/sql_runner.py:121`), the same path the next test already covers. The query-cursor allocations at `sql_runner.py:149` and `:155` are never made to fail, so moving them outside the `try` would leak a connection and pass every unit test. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `tests/unit/test_safety.py` lines 1175-1185: the new `("mysql", "sleep(0)", "Nested MySQL comments")` row in `test_call_after_nested_comment_markers_is_checked` is refused by the nested-comment check (`src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:512`) before any function lookup, so it does not test what the test name describes and repeats the refusal pinned at lines 1125 and 1158. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. `docs/internal/agent/factory.md` line 170: the edited MySQL row of the scheme table says the URL "requires user, host, and database name", but `build_sql_runner` (`src/sqllens/agent/factory.py` lines 250-257) checks only the hostname and username, so `mysql://u@h` reaches `MySQLRunner` with an empty database. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: rewording the table row changes no output of build_sql_runner; git grep -F for docs/internal across *.sh, *.py, *.jq, *.yml, *.yaml, *.toml, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/ and .prflow/skill-extensions/ finds no reader of this page for behavior; docs/internal has no publishing site and vendor-slice.sh:106 strips it -->

[docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md:56] [behavior-inert prose cap] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: first-conjunct held (the judged prose is the sentence at docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md:56; rewording it to scope "as written" to table names and unquoted identifiers changes no output, branch or covered set of apply_rls); limb-one held (git grep -F for row-level-security.md and docs/internal across *.sh, *.py, *.jq, *.yml, *.yaml, *.toml, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/ and .prflow/skill-extensions/ found no tool or agent that reads this page for behavior; AGENTS.md:133 only points agents at docs/internal in general); limb-two held (docs/internal is an internal page with no publishing site: no mkdocs.yml, and vendor-slice.sh:106 strips docs/internal) -->

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Parts that hold: rls.py:236,272,290,298 match table names to rules via .lower() (case-insensitive); the final tree.sql(dialect=dialect, normalize_functions=False) at rls.py:318 passes no normalize/identify flag, and sqlglot generator.identifier_sql (sqlglot 30.26 in the repo .venv, generator.py:2130-2148) lower-cases only when self.normalize is set, so unquoted identifiers are not case-folded; apply_rls raises RlsError only for non-query, parse failure, TABLE shorthand, unresolved protected refs, and bad dynamic values (rls.py:206-313), none keyed on non-ASCII; relations.py:148-154,169-171 sets mysql_fold = (lower_case_table_names != 0) and lower-cases names only then. 
  Part that fails (absolute 'writes identifiers as they were written ... under any dialect'): the injected predicate is built by _predicate (rls.py:165) as exp.column(rule.column, table=qualifier), where qualifier = table.alias_or_name (rls.py:275), a bare string with quote information dropped. sqlglot exp.column -> to_identifier(table, quoted=None) (sqlglot/expressions/core.py:2841-2861, 3133) sets quoted = not SAFE_IDENTIFIER_RE.match(name), with SAFE_IDENTIFIER_RE = ^[_a-zA-Z][\w]*$ (core.py:2828). So a quoted source identifier that is 'safe' is re-emitted unquoted in the predicate. Falsifying input: apply_rls('SELECT * FROM "Orders"', [rule on orders], dialect='postgres') (the criteria file names direct postgres calls of apply_rls) yields FROM "Orders" WHERE Orders.tenant_id = ..., where Postgres folds Orders to orders and no longer matches the quoted "Orders" (same for an alias such as AS "O"). The written identifier is changed in the output. Under dialect mysql a backticked alias containing a supplementary-plane letter (matches \w, but MySQL unquoted identifiers allow only U+0080-U+FFFF) is likewise unquoted. In sqlite and plain mysql the change is semantically harmless but still not 'as written'. The effect is a failing or non-matching query (fail-closed), not a bypass. The doc sentence at row-level-security.md:56 therefore over-claims; 'as written' holds for table names and unquoted identifiers, not for the qualifier in injected predicates. Dispatch had no dependency_sources; sqlglot was read from /Users/the01geek/repos/sqllens/.venv (30.26.0, within the pyproject pin >=30.22,<31). I did not run code.

  </details>

- VC-67: FAIL (suggestion) — The test docstring asserts that PostgreSQL, mysqlx and every other non-MySQL, non-SQLite URL is refused at load. [tests/unit/test_config_schema.py:132]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The docstring at tests/unit/test_config_schema.py:132 says every non-MySQL, non-SQLite URL is refused at load. The validator DatabaseConfig._supported_url_scheme (src/sqllens/config.py:109-116) accepts a value when '://' is present and the lowercased scheme is 'mysql', starts with 'mysql+', or starts with 'sqlite' (line 114). That is a prefix match, so `sqlitefoo://x` is accepted although it is not SQLite. `mysql+://x` is also accepted (empty driver). Both can arrive through a TOML file or the SQLLENS_DATABASE__URL env var. The field description (config.py:66-68) itself says 'a scheme starting with sqlite is still accepted', which confirms the prefix behavior is deliberate and contradicts the docstring's 'every other'. The listed inputs (postgresql, postgres, postgresql+psycopg2, mysqlx, mariadb, empty string, no '://') are all refused, so the docstring is right for those, but not for the absolute wording. The tests in this file do not cover `sqlitefoo://`. A non-str value is rejected earlier by pydantic str typing, so it does not matter here. The criteria file was not consulted because the item is source_authored, so the eligible-item criterion exclusion does not apply.

  </details>
